The e2e journeys (e2e/managed-agent-run.spec.ts, e2e/managed-recovery.spec.ts) are type-checked here but not run; their fixture-mode cases passed 6/6 when authored (MCOMP-25-04) and MCOMP-26 executes and records the endpoint-mode cases.

behavior: A composer send or a queued send returns the managed run its spawn was admitted under (lease, authority, request, attempt, digest, provider, actor, policy revision) and the AI tab keeps it for that turn; a retry or resume is a new admission under the policy current at that moment.
A managed sink refusal survives the process:spawn rejection as a parseable state/code/message (a forged state is refused) and is recorded on the tab from both send paths.

The dispatch ledger answers a run by lease id (IPC enterprise:managedRun, bridge managed_run, maestro-cli managed run): a stopped, released, revoked or restart-unknown run reads back from the durable record; a receipt for another lease is never joined.

The AI tab shows the run state (admitted, running, completed, denied, offline, revoked, unknown) with the host reason and revision and only the recovery the state allows (Stop, Send again, Refresh policy).

Live managed runs are held to the host standing on a timer and after a policy refresh: denied, suspended, revoked, retired or custody-refused revokes the running lease, stopping its process with the reason in the ledger.

contractMappings.remaining: The run view is a Maestro-local projection of the admission and the dispatch receipt; no wire operation or advertised capability was invented in this phase and contract-coverage.json gained no entry. Production admission still requires authenticated negotiated authority.
